blogs.title: Beyond the Classic Triad: Recognizing Telomere Biology Disorders in Young Adults Without Mucocutaneous Signs
blogs.description: This post challenges the traditional diagnostic heuristic for Dyskeratosis Congenita (the classic triad of nail dystrophy, oral leukoplakia, and skin pigmentation). We will analyze why relying solely on physical exam findings leads to missed diagnoses in young adults and explore the 'silent' presentation of Telomere Biology Disorders (TBDs) where multisystem fibrosis and cytopenia precede any visible mucocutaneous changes.

blogs.title: The PARN Paradox: Decoding Monoallelic vs. Biallelic Mutations in Telomere Disorders
blogs.description: While biallelic *PARN* mutations are historically linked to severe pediatric dyskeratosis congenita, this case illustrates a distinct phenotype driven by a monoallelic variant. We will dissect the genotype-phenotype correlations for *PARN*, discussing how haploinsufficiency can manifest as adult-onset pulmonary fibrosis, hepatic cirrhosis, and bone marrow failure, blurring the lines between recessive and dominant inheritance patterns.

blogs.title: When Deficiencies Are Just the Tip of the Iceberg: Unmasking Genetic Marrow Failure Behind Nutritional Anemia
blogs.description: Our patient presented with severe B12/folate deficiency mimicking nutritional anemia. This article explores the concept of 'functional reserve': how underlying telomere biology defects reduce the hematopoietic stem cell pool's resilience, rendering otherwise treatable nutritional deficits catastrophic. We will discuss when to suspect an inherent genetic cause when a patient fails to respond adequately to repletion therapy or presents with disproportionate multiorgan involvement.

blogs.title: Silent Fibrosis: Hepatic and Pulmonary Involvement as Hallmarks of Undiagnosed TBDs
blogs.description: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is increasingly recognized as a manifestation of TBDs, but hepatic fibrosis is often overlooked until late-stage cirrhosis develops. This post reviews current registry data linking *PARN* mutations to liver stiffness and fibrosis independent of alcohol or viral etiology. We will discuss screening strategies (transient elastography) for young patients with unexplained liver enzymes or pulmonary symptoms.

blogs.title: The Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS): Navigating Diagnostic Ambiguity in Rare Genetics
blogs.description: Genetic sequencing identified a monoallelic *PARN* missense variant classified as a VUS. This educational piece focuses on how clinicians should interpret VUS results in the context of strong clinical phenotypes. We will walk through ACMG/AMP criteria application (PM1, PM2, PP3) used in this case to upgrade clinical suspicion despite the lack of definitive pathogenic classification, emphasizing that clinical correlation can sometimes outweigh ambiguous molecular labels.
